# Dependency set for the `python-tests` merge gate.
#
# The workflow previously ran:
#     pip install -r requirements.txt 2>/dev/null || pip install pytest ...
# There is no `requirements.txt` at the repo root, so that line ALWAYS fell
# through to the four-package fallback and swallowed the error while doing it.
# That is why `pydantic` and `jsonschema` were missing in CI and why real test
# modules reported as collection errors rather than as passing or failing tests.
#
# This file is installed with no `||` fallback and no `2>/dev/null`: if it is
# missing or unresolvable the job now fails loudly, which is the point.
#
# Contents are evidence-based — derived by parsing the imports of all 264
# `test_*.py` files in the repo, not guessed.

pytest
pytest-asyncio

# Imported by the test suite (file counts from the import scan):
httpx                 # 45 files
fastapi               # 34 files
pyyaml                # 20 files (imported as `yaml`)
numpy                 # 12 files
jsonschema            # 8 files
nats-py               # 4 files (imported as `nats`)
python-jose           # 4 files (imported as `jose`)
requests              # 3 files
pydantic              # 2 files
pydantic-settings     # graph-linker conftest imports it at config time
websockets            # 2 files
typer                 # 2 files
prometheus-client     # 2 files
aiohttp               # hf-research-agent and other service modules

# From pmoves/pyproject.toml [project.optional-dependencies] dev
cryptography
google-auth-oauthlib>=1.2.0

# NOT found by the import scan, and could not have been: nothing imports
# `multipart` by name. FastAPI requires it at ROUTE-DEFINITION time for any
# endpoint declaring Form(...), so `import main` raises
#   RuntimeError: Form data requires "python-multipart" to be installed.
# before a single test runs. flute-gateway/main.py has such an endpoint, so its
# whole test module failed at collection.
#
# Worth recording as a limit of this file's method: deriving the dependency set
# by parsing test imports is sound and evidence-based, but it is structurally
# blind to packages that are never imported by name and are instead required at
# runtime by a framework. When a test module fails at import with a package name
# in the message, check here before assuming the service's packaging is wrong.
python-multipart      # fastapi Form() dependency; imported by no test directly

# Same blind spot as python-multipart above, found the same way. `slowapi` is
# imported by pmoves/services/content-provenance-gate/main.py and by no test, so
# the import scan could not see it, and test_content_provenance_gate.py failed at
# import with ModuleNotFoundError. That failure was invisible for months because
# the file sat in the `pmoves/tests [1]` chunk, which times out and whose results
# were discarded wholesale until the per-file fallback in this same change.
# Installing this is necessary but not sufficient — the tests then fail on auth
# and need real work in that service — but a missing dependency should not be
# what is hiding that.
slowapi               # content-provenance-gate rate limiter; imported by no test directly

# Deliberately NOT installed: torch (3 files). It is a multi-GB download for
# three tests and would dominate gate runtime. Those modules stay recorded in
# the ratchet baseline as collection errors rather than being hidden — see
# pmoves/configs/pytest_ratchet/_known_failures.yaml.
